overview: This 597-page file traces Allied efforts to reshape Japanese industry after World War II. Industrial inventories and technical studies inform negotiations over civilian production limits, industrial disarmament, and reparations. Policy papers, diplomatic correspondence, plant lists, and directives record how U.S. officials, SCAP, and the Far Eastern Commission selected facilities for retention or removal while weighing Japan’s economic recovery and other countries’ claims.
interest: Detailed plant lists and successive policy drafts let historians trace how technical estimates became occupation decisions and reparations claims.
